change: Version 2 drops version 1's language parity gate (D's English/Korean gap at most 0.05, in recall and coverage) at the repository owner's direction: Jev is built and measured in English only, every input reaching it through the translator, and Korean input left Jev's decisions near 50%. The other seven gates are version 1's, unchanged. Korean-to-English meaning is the translator's to measure, not Jev's.
description: Stage 10's release targets, frozen before any held-out run. Changing one after a failure is a new version and a new evaluation, never an edit of this one. `tool/eval/report.py` reads them: `min`/`max` compare a point estimate, `improvement` needs the estimate at the target and the 95% interval (resampled by intent) above zero, `non_inferiority` needs the interval's lower end at or above the target, `zero` needs no observed case. A result whose interval does not settle it is inconclusive, and any result on labels no person reviewed is provisional.

gates.label: Deterministic integrity
gates.about: cross-repository leaks, fabricated accepted locators, unauthorized executions, duplicated actions

gates.label: Graph benefit
gates.about: supporting-evidence recall on bridge intents, D over A

gates.label: Overall recall
gates.about: supporting-evidence recall over every evidence intent, D against A

gates.label: Answer support
gates.about: D's unsupported-claim rate at least 25% below A's (zero if A's is zero), coverage no lower

gates.label: Decision quality
gates.about: allowed useful choice on the held-out action fixtures; execution authority violations are the integrity gate

gates.label: Added latency
gates.about: D's p95 retrieval and verification time over A's, same workload

gates.label: Operating ceiling
gates.about: runs over their deadline, call or token allowance; an unknown price stays unknown
